column1: # Declared exceptions to the contrast rule in w1_contrast_verify.sh.
# This file exists for the same reason hbh.convention_exemptions does: a rule
# whose exceptions live inside its own test file is a rule that every batch
# quietly edits. An exception here is a written debt with a named reason, and
# deleting a line is a deliberate act that the suite then enforces.
# The floor on an exempt pair is TODAY'S measured ratio, not the standard.
# That makes it a ratchet, not a pass: the pair cannot get worse without the
# suite failing, and the moment the decision below is taken the line is
# deleted and the pair is held to 4.5:1 like every other.
# Columns, tab-separated:
#   foreground-token   background-token   min-ratio   reason
# ONE open decision, three pairs.
# The brand panel and the ops sidebar sit on a gradient that runs
# teal-900 (#1E5D64) -> teal-700 -> teal-600 (#2A7680). The on-dark text
# scale clears 4.5:1 against the dark end and fails against the light end:
#     on-dark-2 on teal-900  5.26:1  ok        on teal-600  3.69:1  fails
#     on-dark-3 on teal-900  3.94:1  fails     on teal-600  2.77:1  fails
# on-dark-3 is text in all eight of its declarations - 11px and 11.5px:
# the sidebar user's subtitle, the sign-in panel footer, the live player
# caption, and the "next session" label. At 2.77:1 that is the worst pair
# in the system, and it is the one to fix first.
# Two fixes, both design decisions and neither the test's to make:
#   a) Lighten the on-dark scale. Reaching 4.5:1 against teal-600 needs
#      roughly #E4F1F4, which collapses the gap to --hbh-on-dark (#FFFFFF)
#      and leaves the on-dark scale with one tier instead of three, in both
#      apps.
#   b) Darken the ground under the text. End the gradient at teal-700, or
#      keep teal-600 only where no small text lands on it. This preserves
#      the scale but changes a signature surface - the staff sign-in panel
#      and the ops sidebar.
# (b) is the better direction: the scale is used in four places and the
# gradient in two. But it is a visual call on the sign-in screen, so it
# waits for a person.
# Owner: design decision, OPEN.
hbh-on-dark-2
column4: gradient light end; open decision in this file's header

column1: hbh-on-dark-3
column4: worst pair in the system; fix first - see header

column1: hbh-on-dark-3
column4: same scale, dark end; resolved by the same decision

column1: # Not debt - a threshold correction.
# teal-300 is 3.84:1 on teal-900, and the token's own comment calls it
# "legible on the dark sidebar". It is legible: all three of its uses are
# non-text, or text above the large-text size, and the WCAG floor for those
#     hbh-admin.css:286  a 17px icon in the sign-in panel   (graphic, 3:1)
#     hbh-app.css:434    the chart bar fill                 (graphic, 3:1)
#     hbh-shared.css:232 .hbh-wm--on-dark - the wordmark    (display lockup)
# If it is ever used for running text, delete this line first.
hbh-teal-300
column4: graphic and display lockup only; 3:1 is the correct floor
